decisions.reason: An accelerator program for green startups lies outside the firm's core machinery business and ties up management attention, and it has shown no revealed value beyond a home-page mention, so abandoning it frees resources for the core WASTX options.
The bio-based CO2-negative bitumen binder is still highly uncertain but cheap to keep listed on its own page, so the option is worth holding until market feedback resolves its value.

The WASTX Cleanic is a recent launch co-developed with ERMAFA, which shares the cost of the option, and it fits the core waste-treatment technology, so it should stay open while demand from the medical waste market becomes clear.

The WASTX Snowflake is the newest core mechanical recycling product and works both as a pretreatment stage and as a stand-alone plant, giving it flexible upside at low marginal cost, so it clearly warrants keeping.
